newsitem.title: UK: UK insurance body calls for plain English.
newsitem.headline: UK insurance body calls for plain English.

text.p: The chairman of the London international insurance and reinsurance market association (LIRMA) on Friday called for simpler wording and a more standardised claims settlement procedure in the London insurance market.
Speaking to the British Insurance Law Association, Philip Marcell said such changes would speed processes and help the industry streamline costs.

"If there are two aspects of our business which give rise to concern and then litigation, they are the claims agreement and settlement process and the production of gobbledegook wordings," said Marcell.
He said LIRMA was in contact with Lloyd's regarding an electronic clauses and wordings database.
